Partir de Gm3, meilleur candidat mesuré (0,05404 s; score 0,68024). Tester l’ajout de la parallélisation des lignes de bornes Z de T1, qui complète les tuiles racines indépendantes. T1 a mesuré 0,06203 s avec les deux niveaux parallèles, mais ce gain n’établit pas un bénéfice supplémentaire sur Gm3; l’essai « lignes seules » était proche de la baseline. Conserver Gm3 comme référence et mesurer la combinaison sans présumer d’additivité.

decision.rationale: Partir de l’intégration 4246, valide à 0,05346 s. Tester sélectivement l’accumulation de lightColor*k avant l’application de l’albédo par canal : cette transformation distincte est valide seule, mais son temps de 0,11357 s ne prédit pas son effet dans le shading optimisé. Conserver 4246 comme référence et vérifier correction et performance aux budgets de threads prévus; ne pas présumer d’un gain.

Comparer le shading de 32c à la base actuelle avant de décider s’il apporte une transformation distincte. L’essai est valide mais légèrement plus lent que 1f seul; une idée complémentaire peut néanmoins être utile dans l’intégration actuelle.

G-2 (ac6f92b8def44472) est valide à 0,052859 s, contre 0,053461 s pour G-1 (4246b59c45384fc2). Le code de 32c répète une voie de normalisation déjà remplacée par le calcul direct mieux mesuré de Gm3; son résultat isolé est aussi plus lent que les intégrations. Je ne vois pas d’autre transformation distincte justifiant un essai supplémentaire. Demander la confirmation indépendante du meilleur candidat validé; ne pas présenter le petit gain mesuré comme confirmé.

children.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, compare parallel work decomposition while preserving the requested thread budget: worksharing the independent coarse-root tiles (including static versus dynamic scheduling) and parallelizing the independent base-level depth-bound rows in MinMaxZTree::Update. Measure each approach independently and, if useful, measure a combination rather than assuming additive gains; higher tree levels still depend on completed lower levels. Keep culling and shading algorithms unchanged, pass run()'s thread count as an upper bound, avoid unnecessary overhead at one thread, and preserve disjoint writes. Validate full output and correctness at 1 and 4 cores, including altered light colors.
children.subject: Parallelize independent coarse tiles within the requested thread budget

children.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, investigate reducing recursive culling and hierarchy work in MinMaxZTree, SplitTileMinMax, IntersectLightsWithTileMinMax, and traversal. In addition to tile granularity and conservative plane-test optimizations, compare stopping subdivision for tiles with small nonzero light lists against continuing to the leaves; measure saved traversal/culling against the added per-pixel light work. Preserve conservative culling, current-frame depth-bound recomputation, and correctness for dimensions not supported by a chosen tile layout. Do not add parallelism or change ShadeTileC in this branch. Validate both core counts and altered light colors.
children.subject: Reduce recursive hierarchy and conservative light-culling overhead

children.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, focus on ShadeTileC's per-pixel BRDF evaluation: investigate safe reuse of pixel and light values, reducing expensive normalization/pow work, and/or row-wise compiler vectorization. Preserve the original shading semantics closely; any approximation must meet the one-intensity-level tolerance on all correctness checks, including altered light colors, and must not rely on a single expected frame. Do not change the tile-culling strategy or introduce threading in this branch; measure both 1- and 4-core cases and retain a portable path unless the frozen build proves a specific ISA is available.
children.subject: Optimize per-pixel shading math and row-wise vectorization

decision.rationale: Examiner le programme Gm3 avant de choisir une intégration mesurée; sa validité et ses performances ne dispensent pas d’examiner le code réel.

Partir de Gm3, meilleur candidat mesuré (0,05404 s; score 0,68024). Tester l’ajout de la parallélisation des lignes de bornes Z de T1, qui complète les tuiles racines indépendantes. T1 a mesuré 0,06203 s avec les deux niveaux parallèles, mais ce gain n’établit pas un bénéfice supplémentaire sur Gm3; l’essai « lignes seules » était proche de la baseline. Conserver Gm3 comme référence et mesurer la combinaison sans présumer d’additivité.

children.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, compare parallel work decomposition while preserving the requested thread budget: worksharing the independent coarse-root tiles (including static versus dynamic scheduling) and parallelizing the independent base-level depth-bound rows in MinMaxZTree::Update. Measure each approach independently and, if useful, measure a combination rather than assuming additive gains; higher tree levels still depend on completed lower levels. Keep culling and shading algorithms unchanged, pass run()'s thread count as an upper bound, avoid unnecessary overhead at one thread, and preserve disjoint writes. Validate full output and correctness at 1 and 4 cores, including altered light colors.
children.subject: Parallelize independent coarse tiles within the requested thread budget

children.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, investigate reducing recursive culling and hierarchy work in MinMaxZTree, SplitTileMinMax, IntersectLightsWithTileMinMax, and traversal. In addition to tile granularity and conservative plane-test optimizations, compare stopping subdivision for tiles with small nonzero light lists against continuing to the leaves; measure saved traversal/culling against the added per-pixel light work. Preserve conservative culling, current-frame depth-bound recomputation, and correctness for dimensions not supported by a chosen tile layout. Do not add parallelism or change ShadeTileC in this branch. Validate both core counts and altered light colors.
children.subject: Reduce recursive hierarchy and conservative light-culling overhead

children.objective: In src/candidate.cpp, focus on ShadeTileC's per-pixel BRDF evaluation: investigate safe reuse of pixel and light values, reducing expensive normalization/pow work, and/or row-wise compiler vectorization. Preserve the original shading semantics closely; any approximation must meet the one-intensity-level tolerance on all correctness checks, including altered light colors, and must not rely on a single expected frame. Do not change the tile-culling strategy or introduce threading in this branch; measure both 1- and 4-core cases and retain a portable path unless the frozen build proves a specific ISA is available.
children.subject: Optimize per-pixel shading math and row-wise vectorization
